page: The Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configuration built on the EDSv4 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores, leveraging two threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 504.0 GB, establishing a high density of 31.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included. Local storage is bundled, providing 2,577 GB of solid-state disk space.

Benchmark results reflect steady mid-tier execution speeds aligned with the 16-vCPU footprint. The instance scored 1,368.0 on Geekbench single-core and 7,775.0 on multi-core testing, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 17,846.77 and database operations rating of 7,126.2. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieved 1,486.38 in single-core and 15,092.71 in multi-core metrics. Memory performance demonstrated high throughput, delivering 842.48 GB/sec for small cached reads, 101.42 GB/sec for large uncached reads, and 72.7 GB/sec for large uncached writes. In application-level testing, the platform achieved 14.55 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 12.3 GB/sec in static web serving, while showing weaker prompt processing performance of 29.58 tokens per second on medium 7B parameter language models.

The primary architectural advantage of the E64-16ds_v4 lies in its constrained compute core profile. Maintaining the large 504.0 GB memory pool and 2,577 GB local SSD capacity of a full chassis while restricting active vCPUs to 16 allows organizations to optimize per-core database software licensing costs. The main tradeoff is the reduced compute and parallel processing ceiling compared to 64-vCPU counterparts. Consequently, this server is suitable for memory-dense enterprise databases, large in-memory caching solutions like Redis, and intermediate ETL pipeline buffering where memory capacity dictates operational stability rather than raw core scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz with x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It provides an extensive memory capacity of 504.0 GB, resulting in an allocation of 31.5 GB per vCPU, alongside 2,577 GB of integrated local SSD storage. The configuration lacks hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles place both single-core and multi-core compute throughput within average distributions, complemented by sustained uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 100 GB/sec and Redis throughput reaching 14.55 million operations per second. By constraining core counts while preserving memory and storage capacity, this instance offers favorable software licensing cost efficiency for memory-bound relational database engines, large in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing.
